clue.text: Henry waded in wildly with a blow to the face

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: the letters of waded in are thrown about wildly into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man called Henry splashes frantically through water and gets punched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges WADED IN to EADWIND after H. The definition is fair because a wind of this kind blows straight into your face.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing against the direction of travel strikes a walker or cyclist full in the face.

clue.text: Ruin with dead low returns

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for low comes back the other way

parts.note: to low is to moo, the noise cattle make

explanation.surface: Ruin arrives along with a deadly depression coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MOO into OOM, which follows D.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean destruction or a terrible fate.

clue.text: Sign of supreme Queen

parts.note: arch means chief or supreme, as in arch-enemy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A token of the monarch's absolute authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a sign of the zodiac: Sagittarius, the Archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius, a zodiac sign, is pictured as a bowman.

clue.text: Box for most of surplus

indicators.note: most of says the word for surplus loses its final letter

parts.note: spare means extra or surplus

explanation.surface: A container set aside for nearly all the extra stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SPARE to SPAR. 'Box' is the verb, to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to practise fighting with fists, as boxers do.

clue.text: 100+ in carriage? That's some vision

indicators.note: in places the number inside the word for carriage

parts.note: carriage is bearing or deportment, and so presence
a little over a hundred: 101 in Roman numerals is CI

explanation.surface: Over a hundred people crammed into a railway coach: quite a sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' is not a railway coach but one's bearing, PRESENCE, and CI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreknowledge of events is a kind of seeing into the future.

clue.text: Very brief indulgent spell about end of July

indicators.note: about means the word for indulgent spell goes round the extra letter

parts.note: a fling is a brief period of self-indulgence

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of July

explanation.surface: A short self-indulgent holiday at the close of July.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurried visit or a quick stop is described with this adjective, meaning short and fast.

clue.text: Ragman?

parts.note: a rag is slang for a newspaper, so a rag man is one who writes for a paper

explanation.definitionFit: Journalists work for newspapers, which are dismissively called rags.

clue.text: Retort from tenor before difficult Bach work

indicators.note: before places the tenor letter ahead of the rest

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: difficult signals the letters of Bach work are knotted into another order

explanation.surface: A tenor's complaint about a fiendishly hard piece by Bach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges BACH WORK into HROWBACK, which follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer back with a quick reply is to return the remark, a verb phrase meaning riposte.

clue.text: Release of prisoner is a state function

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: Freeing an inmate is a governmental duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Early conditional freedom granted to an inmate on promise of good behaviour.

clue.text: Short seemly protest

indicators.note: Short tells us the word for seemly is cut by its final letter

parts.note: demure means modest and seemly

explanation.surface: A brief, polite objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection or show reluctance is a mild form of protest.

clue.text: Austerity exemplified by tough Sunday joint

parts.note: hard means tough
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Belt-tightening shown by a chewy roast at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday joint' looks like a roast of meat, but it splits into S and HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity means severe privation, going without comforts.

clue.text: Beginning to weave words in design meant to deceive?

definitions.text: Beginning to weave words in design meant to deceive?

indicators.note: Beginning to takes the first letter of weave
the letters of words in design are disguised, rearranged to mislead

explanation.surface: Starting to weave deceptive words into a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: W, then 'meant to deceive' rearranges WORDS IN DESIGN into the remaining thirteen letters; the whole clue also defines the answer as a display designed to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting something attractively to hide its true nature is a deceptive outward show.

clue.text: A minor criminal failing

explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile offender is so called, and the adjective also means neglecting a duty, as with an overdue debt.

clue.text: Source of palm-oil, you might say

definitions.text: Source of palm-oil, you might say

parts.words: Source of palm-oil, you might say
parts.note: palm oil is slang for a bribe, money greasing someone's palm, so its source is a secret fund kept for bribes

explanation.definitionFit: A reserve of money set aside for bribes or illicit purposes pays for greasing palms.

clue.text: Effigy, Arabic silver piece

parts.note: a doll is a small figure or effigy of a person

explanation.surface: A statuette and an Arabian silver coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver coins of that name were minted historically, as with Spanish pieces of eight.

clue.text: Amplify enough to come across

explanation.definitionFit: To increase volume on a dial, and to find or appear unexpectedly.

clue.text: Gratification from piano and vocal entertainment

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: vocal says the word for entertainment is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: leisure is free time for amusement and entertainment

explanation.surface: Joy from a piano recital and singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocal' looks like singing, but it signals that LEISURE is heard as LEASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction and enjoyment are synonyms.

clue.text: Items applied to streamers

parts.note: streamers are runny noses or streaming eyes, wiped with cloths

explanation.definitionFit: Pocket cloths are held to streaming noses and eyes.

clue.text: Messenger, Greek deity (and Latin deity initially)

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of Latin and deity

explanation.surface: A divine go-between from Greek myth, with a Roman counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives L and D from 'Latin deity'.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald announced news and proclamations, so the word means a messenger.

clue.text: Carry on about everything English

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the sum is the total, everything

explanation.surface: Continuing to talk about the whole of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up again after a break is to continue.

clue.text: Takes pains making cash in Europe, tons at first

indicators.note: at first puts the letter for tons at the front

parts.note: roubles are Russian money, used in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Struggling to earn money across Europe, with loads of it to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother or make an effort over something is to take pains.

clue.text: Former picture but not the first

indicators.note: but not the first drops the opening letter of the word for picture

parts.note: a plate is a full-page picture in a book

explanation.surface: An old image without its opening part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not the first' removes P from PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means previous, as in the late chairman.

clue.text: They are the ones for details

explanation.definitionFit: Single numbers in arithmetic are ones, and details are small detachments of soldiers.

clue.text: Russian with a role in Ruddigore

indicators.note: with a role in signals that the name is found inside the opera title

explanation.surface: A Russian character appears in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddigore is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; the run ruddIGORe gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian man's name, as with Prince Igor.

clue.text: Root absorbs energy from earth

indicators.note: absorbs means the word for root takes in the letter

parts.note: to plant is to root, fix firmly in the ground
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Roots draw up energy from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' looks like soil, but it is the world, defined in lower case.
explanation.definitionFit: Our world is one of the bodies orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: Pedestrian ride? Come, that must be wrong

indicators.note: the letters of ride come are wrongly ordered and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A walker objects to being offered a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that must be wrong' rearranges RIDE COME.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian also means dull and ordinary, unremarkable.
